text:
Alex Chen: Idea: treat NVMf as a first-class cold tier and use GPUDirect Storage + RDMA to read straight into GPU buffers, avoiding host DRAM staging.

Priya Patel: So evict -> write page blobs to per-tenant NVMe store, metadata in allocator. On fault, RDMA/GDS read into device memory. Sounds promising but first-touch latency may spike.

Jamie O'Neill: latency SLOs are the worry. We should keep a tiny host hot cache and use predictive prefetch (seq-length histograms + model route) to warm NVMe pages for likely long requests.

Sasha Ivanov: API sketch: allocator.migrate(dest='nvme', async=true, namespace='tenantX/modelY/segZ'); allocator.fetch_to_gpu(page, gpu_ptr, modes=['gds','rdma'], prefetch_if_seq_gt=64).

Alex Chen: Security: per-tenant namespaces, KMS encryption-at-rest, ACLs, IO qdepth caps to limit noisy neighbors. GC/compaction to reduce metadata churn.

Priya Patel: Failure modes? NVMe node down -> fallback to host staging or replicate to standby. Need atomic metadata bits for replication status.

infra-bot: checklist: ensure kernel modules for GDS, validate RDMA firmware, NVMf >=2.3, perf smoke tests.

Jamie O'Neill: I'll prototype on dev: 1 GPU + remote NVMe + RDMA switch. Will measure first-touch latency and prefetch effectiveness.

Alex Chen: I'll write a short design note with API, consistency/fallback semantics, cost model, and telemetry needs (per-tenant NVMe IO + migration metrics). Tagging eng-platform for infra constraints. Thanks!
